assessments.rationale: Using recycled monomaterial PP maximizes the ease and quality of recycling (parameter d) [Page 79] and avoids multi-material bonding or composite structures which are highly detrimental to material recovery (parameter e) [Page 79]. Furthermore, monomaterial PP reduces microplastic and nanoplastic release during end-of-life shredding (parameter p) [Page 80] compared to fiber-reinforced composites, and minimizes waste generation (parameter r) [Page 80] by ensuring a high-purity recycled material output.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Durability and Use stage (monomaterial PP has lower tensile strength and impact resistance compared to ABS or fiber-reinforced composites, potentially reducing the physical lifespan under heavy mechanical stress).

options_evaluated: Threaded metal fasteners with brass inserts
assessments.rationale: This method facilitates non-destructive disassembly, supporting ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (parameter c) [Page 79, Page 14]. It avoids permanent adhesives that are detrimental to recycling (parameter e) [Page 79], reduces the energy and resource consumption required during manual or automated dismantling at end-of-life (parameter g) [Page 79], and minimizes waste generation from damaged parts during disassembly (parameter r) [Page 80].
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing stage (adhesives and ultrasonic welding allow for faster, lower-cost automated assembly and simpler molds).

options_evaluated: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with rare-earth magnets
Synchronous reluctance motor without permanent magnets
assessments.recommendation: Synchronous reluctance motor without permanent magnets
assessments.rationale: Eliminating permanent rare-earth magnets avoids technical solutions that are highly detrimental to the recycling and recovery of clean steel and copper fractions (parameter e) [Page 79]. This enhances the quality of material recovery (parameter d) [Page 79] and reduces the overall environmental and material footprint in end-of-life treatment (parameter m) [Page 33, Page 80] by avoiding complex chemical extraction of neodymium/dysprosium.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use stage (BLDC motors with rare-earth magnets typically offer higher efficiency and power density, leading to lower energy consumption during the use phase).

options_evaluated: Active cooling with dedicated fan and heat sinks
Passive cooling via integrated aluminum housing fins
Phase-change materials (PCM) encapsulated in plastic casing
assessments.recommendation: Passive cooling via integrated aluminum housing fins
assessments.rationale: Passive cooling avoids complex multi-material components like encapsulated PCMs or electronic cooling fans, which are detrimental to recycling (parameter e) [Page 79]. It simplifies end-of-life sorting and separation, improving recyclability (parameter d) [Page 79], and reduces the amount of hazardous or complex electronic waste generated (parameter r) [Page 80].
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Performance/Design stage (passive cooling requires a larger surface area or heavy metal fins, which increases the initial material footprint and product weight).

options_evaluated: Modular design with separate power, motor, and filtration modules
Semi-modular design with hardwired electrical connections
assessments.recommendation: Modular design with separate power, motor, and filtration modules
assessments.rationale: A modular architecture directly enables ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (parameter c) [Page 79, Page 14] by allowing separate modules to be replaced or serviced. It prevents technical solutions that are detrimental to reuse and recycling (parameter e) [Page 79] and minimizes waste generation (parameter r) [Page 80] since only faulty modules are discarded rather than the whole vacuum cleaner.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing and Cost stage (modular architectures require more internal connectors, housing interfaces, and assembly steps, increasing production costs and complexity).

options_evaluated: Removable and standardized Li-ion battery pack
assessments.rationale: A corded design completely eliminates battery end-of-life issues, avoiding hazardous waste generation (parameter r) [Page 80]. It avoids the complex, high-impact recycling processes of lithium-ion cells, which is highly beneficial for the environmental footprint of end-of-life treatment (parameter m) [Page 33, Page 80] and avoids solutions detrimental to easy recycling (parameter e) [Page 79].
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use stage/User Experience (corded vacuums significantly limit portability, maneuverability, and user convenience compared to cordless models).
